vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: macro-helper
Version: 1.0.4

The macro-helper skill bundle is a legitimate tool designed to assist users with Excel VBA development. The primary script, scripts/macro.sh, acts as a template generator that outputs static VBA code snippets, debugging tips, and optimization advice based on user input. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection; the instructions in SKILL.md and tips.md are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of providing VBA assistance.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and requested resources are consistent with an Excel/VBA macro helper; nothing in the package attempts to access unrelated credentials, install external software, or exfiltrate data.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (VBA/macro helper) align with the included assets: SKILL.md, tips, and a shell script that emits VBA examples/templates/explanations. The skill does not request unrelated binaries, env vars, or cloud credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to run bash scripts/macro.sh <command> to generate/explain/debug/convert/optimize VBA code. The script only prints VBA examples and guidance; it does not itself read user files, access environment variables, or call external endpoints. Note: generated VBA examples include Outlook and filesystem operations (e.g., sending email, attachments, opening files) — these are expected for a macro helper but are potentially sensitive when executed by the user. The agent instructions do not instruct broad data collection or exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only with an included helper script). No downloads, no package installs, and no archives/extract operations — low install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The sample code references application objects in VBA (Excel/Outlook) which is appropriate for the stated purpose and does not imply hidden credential requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent presence or modify other skills. It is user-invocable and allows normal autonomous invocation, which is the platform default and acceptable here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims — generate and explain VBA macros. Before using: review any generated VBA thoroughly before enabling macros (macros can access files, send email, or delete data). If you plan to run generated code that integrates with Outlook or the filesystem, test it in a copy of your workbook or a sandbox environment. Confirm the publisher/site (bytesagain.com) if you want provenance, and inspect the full scripts in the package yourself; although the provided script prints templates only, generated macros could perform sensitive actions when pasted into Excel and executed.
